# parity-fuzz --mode funclist baseline: normalized signatures of KNOWN gaps.
# A divergence whose signature is here is allowed; a NEW one fails CI.
# Regenerate: parity-fuzz --mode funclist --count N --verify 3  (copy NEW-signature lines).
#
# No known gaps — 4000 cases run clean. Covers function LISTING: `functions f`,
# `functions`, `functions -- f`, `typeset -f f`, `whence -f f`, `which f` — all
# of which funnel through printshfuncnode (c:Src/hashtable.c:914).
#
# This mode is about how zsh PRINTS a function back, not what the function does
# (that is `func`). The distinction matters because C never echoes the source it
# was handed: it stores the body as compiled wordcode and renders it back with
# getpermtext (c:954). The printed form is therefore a contract with its own
# rules, and it is meant to be re-parseable — which is the point of `functions`.
#
# The divergence this mode found was a real port bug and was FIXED:
#
#   1. zshrs only has an Eprog for zwc-loaded functions; shell-defined ones keep
#      their raw source in `hn.body`, so printshfuncnode could not call
#      getpermtext and instead ran ~500 lines of hand-rolled text
#      canonicalization — a from-scratch reimplementation of the deparser,
#      walking the body char-by-char tracking quote and brace depth. It drifted,
#      as a reimplementation of a 300-line C renderer will:
#          f() { for i in 1 2; do print $i; done }
#              zsh  `for i in 1 2\ndo\n\tprint $i\ndone`   was `for i in 1 2\ndo print $i\ndone`
#          f() { (print s) }
#              zsh  `(\n\tprint s\n)`                      was `(print s)`
#          f() { g=inner }
#              zsh  `g=inner ` (trailing space)            was `g=inner`
#          f() { { print x } always { print y } }
#              zsh  `{\n\tprint x\n} always {\n\tprint y\n}`
#                                                          was `print x } always { print y`
#      7 of 12 hand-checked bodies diverged. The last one is not cosmetic: the
#      listing is no longer valid zsh.
#
#      The trailing space after `g=inner` is not a typo in zsh — taddassign
#      appends ' ' after every assignment value (c:Src/text.c:203-204) and,
#      unlike taddlist (c:170-179, which backs over its final space with
#      `tptr--`), nothing ever removes it. The port's taddassign already had it;
#      the emulation simply never went through taddassign.
#
#      The fix routes the raw source back through the REAL deparser —
#      parse_string then getpermtext — instead of re-deriving its formatting
#      rules. The emulation stays as a fallback for bodies the wordcode parser
#      cannot take (its coverage is narrower than the AST parser that executes
#      them), so a parse failure costs the old rendering, not the listing.
#
#      Note parse_string (exec.rs) had ZERO callers before this: the faithful
#      port existed and the live path went around it — the same
#      port-shadowed-by-a-reimplementation shape as substnamedir and
#      typeset_single.
#
# Nothing fuzzed the listing before this mode existed. `func` covers scoping
# semantics and no generator emitted `functions`/`typeset -f` at all, which is
# how the emulation drifted this far behind a green CI.
#
# Bodies are chosen to force a LAYOUT DECISION out of the deparser: loop and
# conditional bodies (`do`/`then` on their own line, body indented beneath),
# subshells and brace groups (`(`/`)` broken out), `always` blocks, nested
# definitions, and assignments. Flat command lists agree no matter how the body
# is rendered and prove nothing — that is precisely why this went unnoticed.
#
# UNBRACED SHORT-BODY form `f() CMD` / `function f () CMD` (verified-correct
# coverage). The mode only ever wrapped bodies in braces (`f() { … }`); the
# braceless short form (c:Src/parse.c:1747-1748 par_list1 — ONE command is the
# body) was never listed. It was a real port bug, now FIXED:
#
#   par_funcdef / parse_inline_funcdef / parse_anon_funcdef took the unbraced
#   arm via par_cmd but left `body_source: None`, so the shfunc carried no raw
#   body and no C Eprog. printshfuncnode then had nothing to render and printed
#   `f () { }` (empty) for EVERY short-form function — `f() print hi` listed
#   with no body at all. The fix captures the raw body slice for the short form
#   the same way the braced arm does (parse.rs:2504). The one subtlety is the
#   lexer's one-token lookahead: pos() AFTER a zshlex is already past the next
#   token, so body_start is recorded BEFORE each advance through `()` and the
#   leading separators (the braced arm sidesteps this because the `{` is its own
#   token and pos() sits right after it). A naive `pos()` capture dropped the
#   body's FIRST WORD (`print hi` listed as `hi`).
#
#   The generator now emits `f () CMD` and `function f () CMD` (single-command
#   bodies only — par_cmd stops at the first `;`) for a fraction of cases,
#   including the nested-anon body `() print anon`, which drives the
#   canonicalizer's recursive re-brace + indent (zsh lists it multi-line braced,
#   not as the raw `() print anon`). All hand-verified equal on both shells.
#
# Two shapes are deliberately NOT generated, both known-divergent for reasons
# upstream of the listing code. Including them would add ~163 signatures (every
# body × verb pair gets its own) for two underlying bugs, and each line would
# then mask a future regression in that shape:
#
#   - `f() { }` — C keeps an empty-but-present body and prints `f () {\n\t\n}`
#     (c:978-984); zshrs's parser stores no body, so printshfuncnode falls to
#     C's `() { }` branch (c:986). Needs the parser to record an empty body
#     distinctly from an autoload stub.
#   - `f() { … } 2>/dev/null` — C stores the function-level redirection as its
#     own Eprog and emits it after the closing brace (c:988-993). The port HAS
#     that emit (hashtable.rs `// c:989`) but par_funcdef never populates
#     shfunc.redir, so it is always None.
#
# Add both to the vocabulary once fixed.
#
# Any divergence here is a regression.
